answer: Each agent resists sybils by computing a sequential delay proof from the epoch signal: 500000 serial hashes (~4 min/core). A second fable identity requires repeating the full serial work, so 100 fakes burn 400 minutes of non-parallelizable CPU. Honest agents pay once; failed proofs that mismatch the signal are rejected, and repeated failures ripple into 24h locks. This makes mass farming cost more time than any reward can offset.
